record.paper_title: 二分決定グラフに基づく計算複雑さに関する未解決問題について
record.original_question: Clarify the computational-complexity relationship between polynomial-size sum-of-products formulas, polynomial-size product-of-sums formulas, and polynomial-size exclusive-or sum-of-products formulas. In particular, with PolySOP and PolyPOS denoting the classes computed by polynomial-size SOP and POS formulas and PolyESOP denoting polynomial-size exclusive-or SOP formulas, how does PolyESOP relate to PolySOP, PolyPOS, and AC^0_1 = PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS, and what is the general complexity-theoretic comparison between SOP and ESOP expressive power?

evidence.quote: 多項式サイズの積和形、和積形の論理式で計算される関数のクラスをそれぞれ PolySOP, PolyPOS と書くと、定義より、AC_1^0=PolySOP∪PolyPOS である。
これらと PolyESOP との関係の解明が今後の課題となるかも知れない。
積和形と積環和形との表現能力の比較については古くから研究されているはずだが、計算複雑さの枠組での一般的な解析結果は知られていないようである。

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a Boolean function f : {0,1}^n → {0,1}, define the following formula sizes:

• A sum-of-products (SOP) formula for f is an OR of ANDs of literals (variables or their negations). Its size is the total number of literal occurrences.
• A product-of-sums (POS) formula for f is an AND of ORs of literals; size is again counted by literal occurrences.
• An exclusive-or sum-of-products (ESOP) formula for f is an XOR of ANDs of literals; size is counted by literal occurrences.

For a family of Boolean functions {f_n}_{n≥1} with f_n : {0,1}^n → {0,1}, say that:
• {f_n} ∈ PolySOP if there exist SOP formulas computing f_n of size bounded by a polynomial in n;
• {f_n} ∈ PolyPOS if there exist POS formulas computing f_n of size bounded by a polynomial in n;
• {f_n} ∈ PolyESOP if there exist ESOP formulas computing f_n of size bounded by a polynomial in n.

Note that PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS equals the class often denoted AC^0_1 of families computable by depth-2 unbounded fan-in AND/OR circuits of polynomial size.

Determine the inclusion relations among the classes PolySOP, PolyPOS, PolyESOP, and PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS. In particular:

(a) Is PolyESOP contained in PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS, or does there exist a family of Boolean functions with polynomial-size ESOP formulas but no polynomial-size SOP formula and no polynomial-size POS formula?
(b) Conversely, is PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS contained in PolyESOP, or does there exist a family with polynomial-size SOP (or POS) formulas but requiring superpolynomial-size ESOP formulas?
(c) More generally, give a complexity-theoretic comparison of the expressive power of SOP and ESOP representations as a function of the number of variables.
artifact.status_search_result: Standard web search did not reveal a known resolution of the relationships among PolySOP, PolyPOS, and PolyESOP as complexity classes. While ESOP minimization and expressiveness have been studied in logic-synthesis contexts, no general complexity-theoretic separation or inclusion between polynomial-size SOP/POS and polynomial-size ESOP families appears to be established in the accessible literature, suggesting the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Fast Heuristic Minimization of Exclusive-Sums-of-Products
status_evidence.snippet: ESOP expressions are XOR sums of products of literals; minimization is studied as a logic-synthesis problem.
status_evidence.claim: ESOP expressiveness studied in logic synthesis, not as a formal complexity class compared to SOP/POS.

status_evidence.title: Exclusive or Sum of Complex Terms expressions minimization
status_evidence.snippet: Work on ESOP-style expression minimization in VLSI design.
status_evidence.claim: No general complexity-theoretic separation between polynomial-size SOP/POS and polynomial-size ESOP families is reported.
